page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core memory ratio. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8481C processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core execution is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation tests. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; both Passmark memory scores and large-block memory bandwidth read/write speeds are positioned in the poor to weak ranges. Conversely, the instance demonstrates average throughput for static web serving and single-threaded compression tasks. It also supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for specialized vector and matrix operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highcpu-4 offers a dedicated compute profile suitable for workloads that require consistent CPU allocation without the overhead of excess memory. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is best suited for lightweight compute-bound tasks, single-threaded processing, static web serving, and basic text processing. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded high-performance computing, or large-scale software compilation due to its constrained memory capacity and lower multi-core scaling.
